title: Prioritize noise-resistant escalation paths and proportional burn throttling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: After the capacity regression on 2026-02-12 we observed repeated burn-rate pagers that were noisy and disproportionally high for small but visible latency spikes. This ticket drives a set of follow-ups: (1) implement a tiered, rate-limited paging path that defers page routing unless impact crosses a volatility-aware threshold; (2) introduce proportional burn throttling to avoid immediate escalation from transient spikes; (3) add a lightweight anomaly heuristic and dashboard to help operators distinguish capacity regressions vs. noisy single-request bursts.

Context and motivation: The incident postmortem (https://confluence.redwood/inference/postmortem/2026-02-12-capacity-regression) identified two vectors for pager fatigue: sensitive short-window burn alerts (1m) and identical-pageing routes for all teams. Pager storms caused SRE context-switching, delayed containment, and obscured real regressions. We want to keep detection sensitivity for real outages while cutting false-positive page volumes.

Goals:
- Reduce P0/P1 paging volume from SLO burn alerts by 60% for transient spikes under 5 minutes without increasing time to acknowledge real outages.
- Ensure noisy signals are routed to a non-pager triage queue with automated grouping for 5-minute observation windows.
- Provide operators a simple dashboard to inspect event clusters, example requests, and inferred root-cause score.

Proposed deliverables:
1) Tiered paging flow: local (alerts->Slack) -> team (alerts->email) -> pager (alerts->oncall) where the step to pager is gated by (a) sustained burn above proportional threshold, or (b) multiple correlated signals (errors+latency+availability) within a 3-minute window.
2) Proportional burn throttling algorithm implemented in alerting pipeline: compute weighted burn over 1/3/15m windows, apply hysteresis and scale pager probability proportional to signal magnitude.
3) Transient-suppression rule engine: implement rules for deploy windows, autoscaler activity, and known maintenance tags to temporarily raise paging thresholds.
4) Operators dashboard and runbook: a Grafana panel that surfaces root-cause likelihood, top 5 request paths, rollout metadata, and a runbook with suggested mitigation steps.
5) Monitoring and guardrails: synthetic canary that validates that throttling does not delay pager for >95th percentile real outages (test harness in https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12456).

Trade-offs and notes:
- We accept some probabilistic suppression of pages in exchange for a large reduction in noise; the proportional model ensures high-severity events remain likely to page.
- This is intentionally rule-based initially (faster rollout) to avoid the operational overhead and retraining needs of a full ML classifier. A separate ticket will evaluate ML-based classifiers after 30 days of rule data.
- We need coordination with the Console team to expose the new gating controls and with the Oncall policy group to update escalation playbooks.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1: design review and interface spec for alert gating (design doc + sequence diagrams).
- Week 2: implement throttling module in alert pipeline and feature flags (staged rollout to staging).
- Week 3: dashboard + runbook + synthetic tests.
- Week 4: gradual rollout to prod under feature flag -> monitor for missed outages -> ramp to 100%.

Links:
- Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood/inference/postmortem/2026-02-12-capacity-regression
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/inference/designs/noise-resistant-paging
- PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12456
- Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/alerts/noise-resistant-paging

Acceptance criteria:
- Pager volume attributable to short-window burn alerts reduced by >=60% within 14 days of rollout (measured on per-team basis).
- No missed P0/P1 incidents attributable to throttling during a controlled fault-injection test (synthetic canary).
- Runbook and dashboard published and acknowledged by Oncall lead.
